messages.content: I have the Washington answer now. They will release me at 3:30 p.m. Wednesday, including the closeout paperwork, and I can leave for Reagan immediately. The exhibition cases are going separately by contracted truck. Please pull up the February 9-13 itinerary and compare the three Wednesday flights again.

The retained Monday and Friday flights are still available for one traveler. For Wednesday, February 11, the Reagan-to-Boston nonstops depart at 6:45 p.m., 8:15 p.m., and 9:35 p.m. Leaving the museum at 3:30 gives you 3 hours 15 minutes before the first departure. Current weekday travel estimates to Reagan are 35-55 minutes, leaving roughly 2 hours 20 minutes to 2 hours 40 minutes at the airport if you depart promptly. Since the cases are not traveling with you, the 6:45 flight now has a practical margin.
Good. Show me all three as complete itineraries, not just the Wednesday prices.

All three use the same Monday and Friday legs: Monday, February 9, Atlanta to Reagan, nonstop, 10:05 a.m.-11:49 a.m.; Friday, February 13, Boston to Atlanta, nonstop, 4:10-7:15 p.m. The only difference is Wednesday. With the 6:45-8:19 p.m. Reagan-Boston flight, the total is $612.40. With the 8:15-9:49 p.m. flight, it is $584.40. With the 9:35-11:09 p.m. flight, it is $566.40. Each option is issued as one three-city ticket for Avery Thompson.
Are those all the same fare type? I need the change, cancellation, baggage, and seat terms before deciding.

Yes. Those totals are Main Cabin on all three segments. Each includes a personal item, one carry-on, and standard seat selection at booking. A first checked bag is $35 each way if purchased separately. The ticket is nonrefundable to the original payment method, but you may cancel before departure for an airline credit. Changes are permitted without a change fee; any fare increase applies, and a lower replacement fare is returned as a credit. Same-day confirmed changes are not included. The ticket must be used in sequence, and missing a segment can cancel the remaining flights.
Is there a cheaper basic fare, and if so, what would I give up?

Basic Economy is available at $507.40 with the 6:45 flight, $479.40 with the 8:15 flight, or $461.40 with the 9:35 flight. It still includes a personal item and carry-on, but no advance standard seat selection, no voluntary changes, and cancellation produces only a partial credit after a $99 deduction. Checked-bag charges are the same. Main Cabin costs $105 more on each itinerary and retains the flexibility I just described.
Keep it in Main Cabin. Between the 6:45 and 8:15, does the 6:45 still meet the airline's recommended arrival time if the drive takes the full 55 minutes?

Yes. A 3:30 departure with a 55-minute drive puts you at Reagan around 4:25 p.m., 2 hours 20 minutes before the 6:45 flight. The airline recommends arriving 2 hours before departure for this domestic trip. That leaves about 20 minutes beyond the recommendation, assuming you can leave at 3:30 as confirmed. The 8:15 flight adds another 90 minutes of cushion for $28 less.
The release time is firm, and I will not have the cases. Take the 6:45 so I reach Boston earlier. Read back every date and city before you ticket it.

The itinerary is for one traveler, Avery Thompson: Monday, February 9, Atlanta to Washington Reagan, departing 10:05 a.m. and arriving 11:49 a.m.; Wednesday, February 11, Washington Reagan to Boston, departing 6:45 p.m. and arriving 8:19 p.m.; Friday, February 13, Boston to Atlanta, departing 4:10 p.m. and arriving 7:15 p.m. All three flights are nonstop and ticketed together in Main Cabin. The total is $612.40.
That is correct. Are standard seats available on all three legs?

Yes. Standard seats are currently available on every flight, with no additional charge. I can leave them unassigned for later selection or assign available seats during purchase. Seat inventory can change until the transaction is completed.
Leave the seats unassigned for now. Use the payment card already saved in the travel account and book the itinerary at $612.40.

Before purchase, please confirm authorization to charge $612.40 to the saved card ending in 1842 and acknowledge that the Main Cabin ticket is nonrefundable, with cancellation to airline credit and changes subject to fare difference.
I authorize the $612.40 charge to the card ending in 1842 and accept those fare conditions. Complete the booking.

Booked. Avery Thompson is confirmed on the three-city itinerary for February 9-13: Atlanta-Washington Reagan, Washington Reagan-Boston on the 6:45 p.m. Wednesday nonstop, and Boston-Atlanta. All segments are Main Cabin, seats remain unassigned, and the card ending in 1842 was charged $612.40. Airline confirmation: G7K4LP. The ticket is nonrefundable; cancellation before departure returns an airline credit, and changes have no fee but remain subject to fare difference.
